title: Soft music, blues and introductions
summary: Barnes says his uncle's band played soft music for surprise parties, and explains blues played with an introduction.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Is that the kind of music your uncle played?

Where? Your uncle. Oh yeah, yeah. He had to talk. That's right, he played for all the, that's soft music too, because in them times they'd play like a surprise party, you understand? Like you had a birthday coming up, well they'd come up and talk with you and wish you a birthday and all that, tell them you go to bed, maybe the wife or friends, somebody who you're with, have it made up. You get a bunch of them, come on here man, knock on the door, excitement, and the band starts playing and they're rushing on you when you open the door man, it's a big excitement. You come together, you've got everything, all the refreshments all together right there. And you're excited, you don't know what to watch.
Did they ever play blues with that kind of a little band? Oh yeah.

In them days, in that time, during that time when the big band started, the bigger band, blues had more of an introduction to it. You see? Had an introduction, but the way it is not all of any tunes is not introduction. Not an ordinary band.
Did you get your clarinet and show us what you mean by an introduction? Well, an introduction is like...

I'll just hum it, either one. Yeah, an introduction is like the old blues, the first blues you have, you're going to play the blues. Three or four times and then it's coming. See? Well that's going on with the old blues. I sing it, I sing it, I sing it. Anything you play, I'll introduce you to the triple beat and the duck, you know, coming on. And it picks up on probably most everything on the chorus. You make a long tune, you have to go over to the chorus and go on over it and come back and go over it again. You get it in the right three or four minutes.
